name: Ascorbyl palmitate

card.summary: A fat-soluble vitamin C ester used as an antioxidant in skincare and food, offered as a stable alternative to ascorbic acid.
card.note: Skincare ingredient; formulation and stability vary by product.

quick.overview:
Ascorbyl palmitate is vitamin C bonded to palmitic acid, which makes it fat-soluble. It is sold as a vitamin C ester and is used as an antioxidant additive in food (E304) and as an ingredient in skincare.
In skincare, vitamin C products are used for brighter, more even-looking skin; this ester form is chosen for compatibility with oils and creams.
quick.how: It appears in serums and creams as an ingredient, used alongside other skincare. Results over time depend on the product.
quick.risks: It is approved as a food additive in the EU, US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand. Skin products can irritate some users.

lead: Ascorbyl palmitate is an ester of ascorbic acid and palmitic acid, a fat-soluble form of vitamin C marketed as vitamin C ester.[1] It is a white to yellowish powder, slightly soluble in water, with E number E304, approved as a food additive in the EU, US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.[1]

Reviews list it among lipophilic antioxidants used to slow oxidation of edible oils.[2] In skincare it is used as an antioxidant ingredient aimed at brighter, more even skin; no published human trials of this specific ester on appearance exist.

chain: Fat-soluble vitamin C form in a cream or serum
Antioxidant activity at the skin surface
angle.text: Used in skincare for vitamin C benefits in an oil-compatible form.

paras: Formed by acylating vitamin C; melts at about 116-117 degrees C and dissolves freely in ethanol.[1]
Food antioxidant and vitamin C source, and a lipophilic antioxidant in oils.[1][2]
No studies found on its effects on skin appearance. Related research is on its role as a food antioxidant.[2]
